In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of customized birthweight centiles is associated with improved detection of small-for-gestational age infants and improved detection of infants at risk of perinatal death.
SGA infants classified by customized birthweight centiles are at higher risk for perinatal mortality than infants classified by population centiles.
SGA infants are at an increased risk for adverse outcomes compared to infants of normal birthweight, regardless of the method used to define SGA.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the customized birthweight centiles are a better method than population centiles to identify SGA infants.

the results of the study indicate that the use of a customized birthweight centile chart is associated with an increased risk of small-for-gestational age (SGA) classification in infants delivered at term, compared with the population-based chart.
the results of this study suggest that the customized centiles may be a more appropriate method of defining SGA than the population centiles, especially in the preterm period.
The main takeaway from our work is that

there is a significant difference between the customized and population-based classification of small-for-gestational age (SGA) and that this difference is influenced by gestational age (GA) at delivery.
there are many different ways to classify small-for-gestational age infants.
customized centile charts can be a useful adjunct in clinical practice for the assessment of fetal growth.
